questions.question: How does the 4-layer cache hierarchy (in-memory → Redis → R2 bootstrap → CDN) coordinate TTLs and invalidation when a single data domain has per-RPC cache tiers (e.g., aviation: fast/static/no-store) AND a pre-computed bootstrap tier (fast/slow with 15/60 min TTLs) AND CDN edge headers — are there freshness inversion scenarios where a stale bootstrap tier shadows newer per-RPC data?

genesis.observation: ARCHITECTURE.md defines a 4-layer cache hierarchy (in-memory → Redis → Upstream) and six cache tiers (fast/medium/slow/static/daily/no-store at 300s-86400s s-maxage) plus a separate bootstrap tier with fast(15min)/slow(60min) R2 TTLs and CDN-Cache-Control headers separate from Cache-Control — no documented invalidation protocol across these layers

questions.question: Why do 80+ Edge Functions use plain JS (no build step, self-contained per file) while server/ code is TypeScript bundled via esbuild at deploy time — does this dual-runtime split (JS entry points bundling TS server libs) create a cognitive maintenance burden where developers must mentally track what runs in the V8 Edge isolate vs the bundled server context, especially given the shared _*.js helpers that are imported by both?

genesis.observation: AGENTS.md states api/*.js are self-contained JS that CANNOT import from ../src/ or ../server/, but server/gateway.ts is bundled INTO Edge Functions at deploy time via esbuild — the actual boundary is not source-level isolation but build-time bundling, creating a confusing dual-runtime mental model

alternatives_considered: Single TypeScript codebase with unified build
Pure server-side API with no Edge Functions
tRPC or Hono for unified runtime

questions.question: The sebuf proto→code generation pipeline (proto/ → buf generate → src/generated/{client,server}/) produces both TypeScript stubs for the browser AND per-service OpenAPI specs, but 8 operational endpoints (auth, MCP, bootstrap, health, etc.) explicitly opt out of the contract system via api-route-exceptions.json — what drives the decision to exclude these endpoints from the proto contract, and how does the team prevent contract drift between proto-defined gateways and hand-written operational endpoints given that lint:api-contract only enforces the presence of generated routes?

genesis.observation: ARCHITECTURE.md states domain intelligence gateways are generated from proto contracts, but operational endpoints like auth/session, MCP, bootstrap/health, notifications are 'hand-written for concerns that don't fit the contract model' — the boundary between contract-covered and contract-exempt is architectural but the rationale for each exclusion is undocumented

alternatives_considered: Extend sebuf to cover all endpoints

questions.question: The system deploys two independent circuit breaker mechanisms — per-domain client-side CircuitBreaker in src/utils/circuit-breaker.ts (maxFailures=2, cooldown=5min, persistCache with 24h stale ceiling) AND server-side idempotency in api/_idempotency.js (SHA-256 request hash, 180s processing marker, 24h completed-response cache) plus a Redis-outage degraded mode for rate limiting — yet there is no evidence of cascading-failure isolation between domains (one broken upstream taking down all 35+ domains) or a bulkhead pattern at the gateway level. How does the system prevent a single failing upstream from degrading the entire multi-domain API surface?

genesis.observation: CLIENT: 40+ per-domain circuit breakers with independent state (src/services/*). SERVER: idempotency layer with processing marker TTL=180s + completed response TTL=24h (api/_idempotency.js). RATE-LIMIT: degraded mode on Redis outage (ARCHITECTURE.md §8). NO gateway-level bulkhead: createDomainGateway serves ALL domains from shared pipeline — a single upstream timeout could block the entire gateway worker

alternatives_considered: Bulkhead pattern with separate worker pools

questions.question: The variant system (full/tech/finance/commodity/happy/energy) uses hostname-based detection (tech.worldmonitor.app → tech) plus localStorage override and controls panel config, map layers, refresh intervals, theme, and UI text — but the 35+ domain API endpoints are identical across all variants, meaning a tech.worldmonitor.app user pays the cold-start cost for aviation/conflict/climate handlers they never consume. Why was the variant boundary drawn at the SPA level rather than also filtering the API surface (e.g., deploying variant-specific Edge Function bundles that exclude irrelevant domains)?

genesis.observation: Variant detection in src/config/variant.ts is purely client-side hostname routing; all 80+ Edge Functions deploy identically regardless of variant — a tech variant user's browser calls the same /api/aviation/v1 endpoints as a full variant user, just doesn't render the panel. The architectural variant boundary stopped at the UI layer

alternatives_considered: Per-variant API gateway with domain whitelist

questions.question: The cross-domain intelligence pipeline (MCP tool registry, A2A endpoint, NLWeb /ask, tool suggestion engine) uses token-overlap scoring (name=3pts, description=1pt, top-5 suggestions) — a purely lexical matching algorithm — to route queries across 35+ domains. Given that ONNX ML models (MiniLM-L6 embeddings, sentiment, NER) already run client-side in Web Workers for headline clustering and correlation detection, why isn't semantic similarity used for tool suggestion instead of token-overlap? Is the lexical approach a deliberate constraint (cold-start bound on Edge Functions, latency budget) or an evolutionary gap?

genesis.observation: ONNX ML pipeline already exists client-side (src/workers/ml.worker.ts: MiniLM-L6 embeddings, vector store, semantic search) but the MCP tool suggestion engine (api/_agent-tool-suggest.ts) uses simple token-overlap scoring — the same repo has both semantic and lexical routing but they are not connected

alternatives_considered: Unified semantic router using existing ONNX models

questions.question: The multi-language SDK strategy (Go/Python/Ruby/CLI via worldmonitor npm package) relies on hand-written SDKs per language plus sebuf-generated OpenAPI specs — but proto-check.yml only verifies TypeScript generated code freshness. Given that proto definitions evolve across 35+ domains, how are the Go/Python/Ruby SDKs kept in sync with the proto contract, and what is the measured gap between a proto change and SDK release across all 4 target languages?

genesis.observation: proto/ defines 35+ service contracts → buf generate → TypeScript stubs + OpenAPI specs. CI checks only TS freshness (proto-check.yml). 3 non-TypeScript SDKs (sdk/go/, sdk/python/, sdk/ruby/) and the npm CLI (cli/) exist but have no documented contract-freshness CI

alternatives_considered: Manual SDK updates tracked by CI

questions.question: The gateway factory (server/gateway.ts) is a 10-stage pipeline (origin check → CORS → OPTIONS → API key → rate limit → route match → POST→GET compat → execute → ETag → cache headers) shared across all domain bundles as a ~3KB shared import, but the RPC_CACHE_TIER map (lines 167-383) and the idempotency/entitlement/MCP-internal-HMAC logic add hundreds of lines that every domain bundle pulls in regardless of whether the domain uses those features. Was the single-gateway-factory decision a deliberate tradeoff (single source of truth vs per-domain minimal bundle size) and was the cold-start budget impact of bundling all-domain logic into each of 35+ Edge Functions ever measured?

genesis.observation: gateway.ts is 1092+ lines with the comment 'This map is shared across all domain bundles (~3KB)' but the actual gateway.ts includes idempotency checks, MCP internal HMAC, entitlements, usage telemetry, direct LLM quota, bbox validation — all of which are bundled into every domain's Edge Function even for domains that don't use those features

alternatives_considered: Per-domain gateways with selective feature imports
Dynamic feature loading at request time
Shared library via Vercel Lambda Layers or ESM module graph
